## 分诊 · `domain:devx` / `priority:p2` / `pm:queue`

**Anchor read, not guessed.** Both options land in gate/QA surfaces — `packages/qa/downstream-contract` (confirmed present on `origin/main` `f1d7872`, 2026-09-05T00:26:22Z) or `check:published-files` ⇒ `domain:devx`.

### Grade — p2

⭐ **The same event has now happened twice, to two different downstream repos, in the same way:**

| seal | consumer | deep import | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17.3.0 `@objectstack/cli` (#13123) | cloud `objectos-runtime` | `dist/utils/console.js` | broken ⇒ `./console` ratified (#13662) |
| the same seal | hotcrm hook-body fidelity harness | `dist/utils/extract-hook-body.js` | broken at type level **and** run time ⇒ `./hook-body` ratified (#15325) |

⇒ **Both were predicted by #13123's own body** (*"ratify the subpath rather than read `dist/` paths"*), and **both were discovered after publish, by the consumer, during an upgrade.** A defect class that is foreseen, unfixed, and paid for twice by downstream repos is measured pull, not a hypothesis. That is what makes this p2 rather than a nice-to-have.

⛔ Not p1: no in-repo breakage, and each occurrence was recoverable by ratifying a subpath — the cost is a broken downstream upgrade and a round trip, not data or availability.

### ⭐ Why nothing in this repo could have gone red — the structural reason, worth keeping

> the deep imports live in **other repositories**, and every in-repo consumer reaches any file through a **relative import, a vitest alias or a `paths` entry** — **inside the monorepo nothing is sealed.**

⇒ This is not a missing test someone forgot to write. **The monorepo cannot observe the property at all**, by construction. Any fix must therefore either import knowledge from outside (option A) or make the act itself loud (option B).

⚠️ And what #15325 already left behind is real but bounded: `packages/cli/test/published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts` packs with `pnpm pack`, unpacks outside the workspace, and resolves the ratified specifiers — pinning the **current** map exactly (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`, `./package.json`). ⇒ A subpath *removed* from `@objectstack/cli` now reds in-repo. ⛔ **It cannot see the next package that gains a map, and it knows nothing about which specifiers consumers actually use.** ⇒ That pin is the floor this card builds on, not a duplicate of it.

### Boundary test

- **A (consumer-specifier ledger)** — adds a gate/test; narrows nothing authorable. ⛔ No manual floor. ⭐ The precedent is already in-tree: `packages/qa/downstream-contract` exists as *"a frozen, representative third-party consumer of `@objectstack/spec`"*, so this is **extending an accepted pattern one level down**, not inventing one.
- **B (`check:published-files` refuses an unlabelled seal)** — **strengthens** an existing GATED gate and adds a changeset requirement. ⚠️ It changes what a PR must carry to land, which touches every package's release path ⇒ **above the trivial line**, and it needs the devx seat's ruling rather than a dev's choice.

### ⭐ A and B answer different questions — and the card says which is which

> **A** is the one that would have caught **#13662 and #15325** specifically; **B** is the one that would have made **#13123 itself** say which doors it closed.

⇒ **A is retrospective coverage of known consumers; B is prospective disclosure of any seal.** ⚠️ **A alone goes stale** — a ledger of hand-curated specifiers only knows what someone remembered to write down, and the third consumer will not be in it. **B alone predicts nothing** — it makes the seal loud without saying who it hits. ⇒ **C (both) is not fence-sitting; it is the only combination that closes both halves.** ⛔ Triage is not ruling it, but if only one is affordable, **B is the one that scales without maintenance** and A is the one that pays back immediately on the two consumers already known.

⚠️ **Cost A honestly before choosing it**: a ledger with no owner rots, and its entries must leave *"only with a recorded consumer-side migration"* — which means a shrink-only discipline and a person who maintains it. ⭐ Give it a `--self-test` with an anti-vacuity anchor: a ledger gate that silently iterates zero entries is exactly the shape #15410 measured this repo full of (**20 of 178** self-tests demonstrably non-vacuous). ⛔ Do not add the 179th.

### ⛔ Boundary — endorsed and restated

**Not** a request to widen any exports map, and **not** to weaken `check:published-files`'s GATED invariant. **Sealing was right in both cases** — #15325's triage and the reporter both say so. ⭐ **The gap is visibility, not policy.** A PR that closes this by re-opening a subpath has solved a different problem.

⛔ Not a claim, not a dispatch — routing only.

Ruling: option A now — a hand-curated consumer-specifier ledger under `packages/qa/downstream-contract` (the accepted third-party-consumer pattern, one level down), each entry = bare specifier + consumer repo + date + the ratifying card, resolved through the workspace package's `exports` map with Node's REAL resolver from OUTSIDE the workspace (the `pnpm pack` + throwaway `node_modules` shape #15325's pin uses), red on the PR that drops a ledgered specifier naming the consumer; shrink-only with a recorded consumer-side migration; an owner line in the ledger header. Seed: `@objectstack/cli/console` (cloud objectos-runtime, #13662), `@objectstack/cli/hook-body` (hotcrm action-sandbox, #15325), `@objectstack/cli/package.json`. ⛔ B (changeset-gated seals in `check:published-files`) is a release-path policy change — NOT in this PR; the dev files it as a decision card with the measured count of past seals it would have refused. ⛔ Root `package.json` and `packages/cli/package.json` are held by other PRs — no edits there; wire the test inside the qa package's own manifest/vitest config. `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched`, assignee set.

## Closing **completed** — both halves have now landed. Nothing remains.

`domain:devx @ objectstack` seat (#6023), session `session_01PU9zBGbH2s2ZtxSyu963M3`, round 1, **2026-09-06T01:2xZ**.

This card proposed three options and was returned to `pm:queue` on 2026-09-05T05:40Z (`5549735891`) carrying only its remainder. That remainder was **#15715**, and it has now landed:

| half | route | landed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **Option A** — consumer-specifier ledger under `packages/qa/downstream-contract`, resolved through the real `exports` map from outside the workspace | PR **#15717** | `1847594de`, 2026-09-05 |
| **Option B** — `check:published-files` refuses an unannounced seal | split to **#15715**, ruled **B1** by the maintainer (`5550130523`, verbatim 「同意」), implemented as the `ANNOUNCED` invariant | PR **#16082** → `64011dd3f`, 2026-09-06T01:22:25Z |

⇒ The card's dispatchable residue is **empty**, so it closes `completed` rather than returning to the queue. ⛔ It is deliberately **not** closed as a duplicate of #15715: #15715 is one of its two halves, not a restatement of it.

### The two halves close different holes, which is why both were worth landing

- **A** reds on the PR that seals a specifier a **named, cited** out-of-repo consumer imports — retrospective coverage of the consumers we know about (#13662's cloud `objectos-runtime`, #15325's hotcrm hook-body harness). It is silent about anyone nobody has written down.
- **B1** reds on the PR that **narrows the resolvable surface at all**, whether or not the consumer is in the ledger — and it discriminates, so the 44-of-51 born-sealed packages that B-as-worded would have demanded boilerplate from are waved through.

Triage's reading on this card (`5548057783`) called it precisely and is worth preserving as the reason the pair exists: *"A alone goes stale … B alone predicts nothing"*, and the structural fact underneath — **inside the monorepo nothing is sealed**, because every in-repo consumer reaches any file through a relative import, a vitest alias or a `paths` entry. Nothing here could ever have gone red on its own; the coverage had to come either from outside knowledge (A) or from making the act itself loud (B1).

`pm:queue` stripped in the same stroke as the close. No assignee to clear.
